data.title: PhysicsWallah shares gain after FY30 growth blueprint; Motilal Oswal sees ₹200 target
data.description:
Shares of PhysicsWallahLtd. were trading around 3% higher on Thursday, November 19, after the edtech company outlined an ambitious growth roadmap for FY30 at its investor day, targeting revenue of ₹9,000-10,000 crore and an EBITDA margin of more than 20%.

The company's revenue target represents an increase from the ₹3,900 crore reported in FY26 and implies a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of at least 25% between FY27 and FY30.

PhysicsWallah also expects its online business to contribute around two-thirds of total revenue by FY30, with the offline segment accounting for the remaining one-third. In FY26, the revenue mix between online and offline businesses stood at 52:48.

The management's strategy is centred on scaling its existing online platform, expanding into adjacent learner categories, improving the profitability of its offline centres and developing artificial intelligence-led products.

The company aims to strengthen its position across India's education market, estimated at around $185 billion-$195 billion, through asset-light offerings spanning K-12 and post-K-12 segments.

What brokerages say on PhysicsWallah

HSBC has maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on PhysicsWallah, with a price target of ₹150. HSBC said the company's ambition to achieve revenue of ₹9,000-10,000 crore and an EBITDA margin of over 20% by FY30, with online operations expected to account for nearly two-thirds of revenue.

Motilal Oswal has a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and a price target of ₹200. It said management's FY30 revenue ambition implies a consolidated revenue CAGR of at least 25% over FY27-FY30.

Motilal Oswal highlighted the company's focus on scaling its online business, expanding into adjacent learner categories, improving offline profitability and building AI-led products.

DAM Capital has a ‘Buy’ rating on PhysicsWallah, with a price target of ₹155. It said that the company's FY30 targets include revenue of ₹9,000-10,000 crore, a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin of over 20% and an online revenue contribution of around two-thirds, compared with 52% in FY26.

The brokerage believes the margin target could be conservative, as it implies a pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin of around 25% for the online business in FY30, below its current run rate of 27%.

On the offline business, DAM Capital expects PhysicsWallah to moderate the pace of new centre additions to 15-30 annually, with greater emphasis on operating performance and quality.

The brokerage estimates online revenue and EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 24% and 35%, respectively, between FY27 and FY29. For the offline business, it projects revenue growth of 15% over the same period, with adjusted EBITDA turning positive from a loss of ₹38 crore in FY27 to a profit of ₹169 crore in FY29.

data.title: Indonesia parliament passes asset forfeiture bill into law
data.description:
Indonesia's parliament approved a new asset forfeiture law in a plenary vote on Thursday, allowing authorities in certain cases to seize assets linked to corruption and other crimes without the need to first secure a criminal conviction.

  • Civil society organisations and protesters had long called for the law to be passed, arguing it would strengthen asset recovery efforts

  • The law aims to remedy limitations in state asset recovery, which was largely dependent on securing a criminal conviction first, said Rini Widyantini, bureaucratic reform minister

  • She said the new rules apply to perpetrators who flee, die, or suffer from permanent illness

  • Authorities may freeze and seize suspected criminal assets before a court decides whether they should be forfeited, according to a parliamentary presentation slide shown during the vote

  • The latest draft of the law was not immediately made public

  • Lawmakers had agreed that the non-conviction mechanism applies only to assets worth at least 1 billion rupiah ($54,885), state news agency Antara reported earlier this month

  • It also applies to crimes linked to corruption, narcotics, and certain fraud offences, including cryptocurrency and online gambling schemes, local media reported

  • The Legal Aid Institute of Indonesia, a non-government organisation, said on Wednesday that the legislation could help fight corruption and recover criminal proceeds

  • But it warned that it granted extensive powers to freeze, seize and manage assets without sufficiently strong safeguards against abuse

  • The organisation cited a November 16 draft of the bill, which Reuters could not immediately verify

($1 = 18,220 rupiah)

data.title: Australian dollar falls after weak jobs data, bonds rally on rate cut hopes
data.description:
The Australian dollar dropped on Thursday after a surprisingly weak jobs print had markets abandon any chance of further rate hikes and double down on bets for rate cuts next year, sparking a rally in bonds to three-month highs.

Data showed Australia's labour market turned decisively weaker in October, shedding jobs for a second straight month. The unemployment rate hit a five-year high of 4.9%, well ahead of the central bank's expectations, as five rate hikes this year to 4.85% worked to curb demand.

Swaps are no longer pricing in any risk of a rate rise from the Reserve Bank of Australia but are expecting lower rates in the second half of next year. A June rate cut is seen at 68%, while a move in August is about fully priced in. (0#AUDIRPR)

The Aussie fell 0.5% to $0.6679, marking the eighth straight session of declines as growing anxiety over the AI trade added to a global equity sell-off. It is closing in on key support at $0.6662, the lowest level this year.

Bonds rallied on the prospects of rate cuts, with three-year bond yields (AU3YT=RR) down 17 basis points to 4.612%, the lowest since August. Ten-year bond yields slumped 12 bps to 4.977%, also a three-month low.

"The RBA face an increasingly worse policy conundrum. Inflation is still way too high... However, the pace of deterioration in the housing market & now the labour market is worrying," said George Tharenou, chief economist at UBS.

"We now expect the first rate cut of -25bps in Aug-27 (was Nov-27). We also now except an easing cycle of -75bps (was -50bps), with the most likely timing additional -25bps rate cuts in Nov-27 & Feb-28."

The kiwi dollar steadied at $0.5494 after finishing little changed on Wednesday. It is perching dangerously close above $0.5485 and $0.5469, with a breach of those levels opening the way to lows last seen in 2009.

The Aussie also lost 0.6% to NZ$1.2156 , the lowest since early September and well off its recent 13-year peak of NZ$1.2601.

Anna Breman, Governor of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, said on Thursday inflation was elevated due to costly fuel and a weaker currency, but an uneven recovery has limited businesses' ability to pass on higher costs.

Swaps now imply a 78% probability that the RBNZ will raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point to 3%, with 80 basis points of tightening priced in by the end of next year. (0#NZDIRPR)

data.title: Thailand central bank chief proposes 1% to 3% inflation target for 2027
data.description:
Thailand's central bank chief is proposing keeping the inflation target range at 1% to 3% for 2027 and said on Thursday he saw no need for an interest rate change for now.

The central bank still expects 2026 economic growth of 2.4%, with third-quarter growth of 2.9% close to its 3.1% forecast, despite revisions to the manufacturing production index, Governor Vitai Ratanakorn told reporters.

  • Interest rates will be kept steady if the economic outlook remains as expected, but decisions will be data-dependent at each meeting, he said

  • The central bank last month left its key interest rate (THCBIR=ECI) unchanged at 1.00%, with the next rate review on December 23

  • The interest-rate differential with the US is only one factor affecting the baht as any Fed rate increase could put some weakening pressure on the currency, Vitai said

  • Dollar movements remain a key driver of the baht, which has weakened but remains in line with regional currencies and the central bank is closely monitoring it, he said

  • Vitai said it was too early to assess US curbs on advanced chip exports, but risks to exports and investment will be monitored

  • The central bank aims to boost SME loan growth next year, Vitai said

data.title: Japanese investors extend foreign bond selling as US rate-hike bets grow
data.description:
Japanese investors sold foreign long-term bonds for a second straight week in the week through November 14, wary of rising US inflation and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials that reinforced expectations of a December rate hike by the central bank.

They withdrew 440.7 billion yen ($2.77 billion) from foreign long-term bonds, marking their eighth week of net sales in the past nine weeks, Ministry of Finance data showed. They did, however, buy a net 190.8 billion yen worth of short-term bills.

Japanese investors have sold a net 5.1 trillion yen in overseas debt securities so far this year, their largest net sales for the corresponding period since 2022.

US Treasuries have seen significant selling by Japanese investors so far this year, with holdings falling to a nine-month low of $1.063 trillion in September. Japan, however, remained the largest non-US holder of Treasuries, according to US Treasury Department data.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield surged 29.4 basis points last week, its biggest increase since April 2025, after a stronger-than-expected US consumer price reading for October bolstered expectations of a December rate hike.

Japanese investors, meanwhile, bought a net 363.1 billion yen worth of foreign equities, marking their fourth net purchase in the past five weeks.

At the same time, foreign investors bought a net 650.1 billion yen of Japanese long-term bonds, extending their buying streak to seven consecutive weeks. They also bought a net 161.8 billion yen of short-term bills.

Japanese stocks, however, witnessed a second consecutive weekly outflow, to the tune of 224.1 billion yen.

($1 = 159.2600 yen)

data.title: Forum unites Hong Kong Business Associations from global markets to explore new opportunities
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov 19, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - 18 November 2026, The 27th Hong Kong Forum, jointly organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) and the Federation of Hong Kong Business Associations Worldwide, brought together over 300 business leaders and representatives of Hong Kong business associations from 29 countries and regions for first-hand insights into Hong Kong's latest developments and emerging opportunities. As part of the HKTDC's efforts to promote Hong Kong's strengths to the international business community, the annual forum was held from 17 to 18 November at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre (HKCEC) and connected Hong Kong's global network of business friends with prominent leaders of leading Hong Kong enterprises and policy experts, complemented by networking activities and local study tours showcasing the city's transformation.

Through keynote speeches and thematic discussions, participants gained insights into China's 15th Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong's first-ever Five-Year Plan and the HKSAR Government's Policy Address, with speakers explaining their implications and highlighting new opportunities for global businesses. China's 15th Five-Year Plan reaffirms the strategic role of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area as a key engine for developing new quality productive forces. Tailored to local conditions and focused on the city's unique strengths, Hong Kong's first Five-Year Plan aims to better align with the national plan. Discussions explored how international businesses can capitalise on these developments through Hong Kong's strengths in finance, trade, innovation and technology, and professional services.

Leveraging Hong Kong's advantages to foster global business connections

Margaret Wong, Chairperson of the Federation of Hong Kong Business Associations Worldwide, said in her welcome remarks: 'In today's rapidly changing business environment, the value of our Federation network is greater than ever. Bringing together members from different countries and regions, our network provides valuable market insights, trusted connections and a strong platform for business exchange.'

Sophia Chong, Executive Director of the HKTDC, said in her opening remarks that, 'Hong Kong released its first Five-Year Plan, setting out a clear and focused course of action guided by growth and innovation. Priorities include consolidating and enhancing Hong Kong's competitive edge, deepening connectivity with the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and fostering an international collaboration network. This and more are what make Hong Kong uniquely positioned to support Chinese Mainland's high-quality development and international engagement, opening new opportunities for partnership.'

Paul Chan, the Financial Secretary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, attended the luncheon on the second day and delivered a keynote speech. He noted that Hong Kong is actively implementing its first Five-Year Plan to strengthen its strategic positioning as the nation's 'four centres and one hub' comprising an international financial centre, trade centre, shipping centre, innovation and technology centre, and an international hub for high-calibre talent. He highlighted Hong Kong's unique role as the world's largest offshore Renminbi business hub and emphasised the Northern Metropolis as a major engine of future growth, providing vast opportunities in innovation and technology, cross-boundary collaboration and talent development.

Harnessing Hong Kong's strengths to drive innovation and industrial upgrading

As Hong Kong's role as a superconnector and super value-adder between the Chinese Mainland and international markets continues to grow, the city is well positioned to help businesses seize opportunities arising from China's 15th Five-Year Plan through its strengths as an international financial centre, trading hub, innovation and technology ecosystem, and professional services platform.

At the plenary session held on the first day of the Forum, 'Capitalising on the 15th Five-Year Plan via Hong Kong's Multifaceted Enterprise Strengths', Dr Hon Stephen Wong, Head, Chief Executive's Policy Unit, The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, said that Hong Kong's first Five-Year Plan seeks to strengthen the city's role as a key link between national and international development by consolidating its traditional strengths while cultivating new growth drivers. As mainland enterprises expand globally and international supply chains become increasingly diversified, Hong Kong is well positioned to develop into a high-value-added supply chain services centre, providing not only trade and logistics support, but also integrated financial, treasury, insurance, legal and dispute resolution services.

The session was followed by a panel discussion featuring Sabrina Fung, Group Managing Director, Fung Retailing Group; Paulo Pong, BBS, JP, Chairman of M+ Museum Board and Board Member of the West Kowloon Cultural District Authority; and Patrick Wong, CEO, Wing Tak (Shipping) Holdings Limited, Chairman, New Asian Travel & Marine Services Limited, and CEO, Tenacity Int'l Group Limited. In addition to Hong Kong's traditional strengths in finance, trade and professional services, speakers explored how the city can enhance its soft power and global influence through arts and culture, creative industries, and international cultural exchanges. Discussions highlighted how Hong Kong's unique blend of Eastern and Western cultures, world-class cultural infrastructure and diverse talent pool can further support businesses in building their brands, connecting with international markets and fostering cross-sector collaboration.

Also held on the first day of the forum, the thematic session 'Harnessing AI for Innovation: Transforming Industries in Hong Kong' featured a special address by Lillian Cheong, Under Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

The session brought together Justin Chan, Founding CEO, Gense Technologies; Dr Lai Lipeng, Co-founder and Chief Innovation Officer, XtalPi; and Paul Loo, Chief Operating Officer, Lalamove, who shared insights on how artificial intelligence is driving transformation and innovation across sectors including scientific research, healthcare technology and logistics, helping enterprises enhance competitiveness and unlock new growth opportunities. The speakers also examined how Hong Kong can leverage its strengths in talent, capital, research capabilities and international connectivity to accelerate the commercialisation and industrialisation of AI technologies, further reinforcing the city's position as a leading innovation and technology hub and a premier centre for artificial intelligence in Asia.

Young entrepreneurs share innovation journeys and vision for a smarter future

On the second day of the forum, the young executive session, 'The Innovative Disruptors Shaping Our Tomorrow', focused on how the new generation of innovation and technology entrepreneurs are leveraging emerging technologies to address market needs and drive industry transformation.

The session featured Sabrina Chu, Founder, PetWell HK Limited; Desmond Ho, CEO, Alpha AI Technology Limited; Jeff Li, Co-Founder & COO, Hay-koze Limited; and Deacon Wong, Co-founder & CEO, GABES Limited. The speakers explored innovative applications in areas such as smart cities, public safety, employee well-being and digital pet services. They also shared how they have leveraged Hong Kong's robust innovation and technology ecosystem and international connectivity to transform innovative ideas into globally competitive business solutions. In addition, they discussed the challenges encountered during their entrepreneurial journeys and how innovation can help create a smarter, more efficient and better-connected future.

One of the highlights of this year's forum was the launch of the Hong Kong Global NextGen Ambassador Programme, which aims to strengthen ties between young members of Hong Kong business associations worldwide and Hong Kong, while nurturing the next generation of association leaders.

The eight-day programme featured leadership exchanges, visits to enterprises and organisations, mentorship sessions and business networking events. Through these activities, participants gained first-hand insights into Hong Kong's latest economic and urban developments while building connections with local business leaders and young professional networks.

This year, the programme brought together eight young representatives from eight Hong Kong business associations worldwide. The initiative seeks to deepen the younger generation's understanding of and connection with Hong Kong, while encouraging them to serve as ambassadors and bridges between Hong Kong and their respective markets, advocating Hong Kong's unique advantages and opportunities to the wider business community.

Delegates explore Hong Kong's innovation ecosystem and future development

To give participants a deeper understanding of Hong Kong's innovation and technology development, future city planning and major infrastructure projects, the organisers also arranged visits to Cyberport, the Kai Tak Sports Park, and the Northern Metropolis, enabling delegates to experience first-hand the city's vibrant momentum in innovation and development.

The Hong Kong Forum is the annual flagship event of the Federation of Hong Kong Business Associations Worldwide. Founded in 2000, the Federation today has a network of 49 business associations with membership of approximately 11,000 business executives and professionals from 38 countries and regions.

data.title: Korean Entertainment Stocks Surge on Hopes of K-Pop's Return to China
data.description:
By Megan Cheah

Shares of South Korean entertainment companies rose sharply after Seoul's agreement with Beijing opened the door for China to potentially loosen rules barring major K-pop acts from performing in the country.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and China's leader Xi Jinping on Wednesday signed a bilateral free-trade agreement on services and investment, covering sectors such as film, during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

The deal suggests that China could be warming up to ending its de facto ban on Korean pop culture, sparking a rally in entertainment stocks.

Kospi constituent Hybe, the company managing boy band BTS, advanced 13% on Thursday. Shares of entertainment and media company CJ ENM, listed on the smaller Kosdaq board, climbed 23%. Television-drama producer Studio Dragon's stock jumped 30%, while K-pop company SM Entertainment gained 10%.

China's informal ban, which Beijing has never officially acknowledged, was imposed in protest of Seoul's decision to deploy a U.S. missile defense system in 2016. Since then, Chinese television networks, streaming platforms and movie theaters had effectively shut out Korean content, while major K-pop acts were largely barred from staging large-scale concerts.

The free-trade agreement has "revived hopes that Beijing will ease its restrictions on Korean entertainment," said Hana Securities analysts Lee Ki-hoon and Kim Chae-hyun in a note. K-pop companies' earnings could rise by around 40% if China eventually allows K-pop concerts to resume, they wrote.

Studio Dragon looks set to be a more direct beneficiary of the South Korea-China deal. "Studio Dragon could earn additional revenue if Chinese streaming platforms...begin airing Korean dramas they have already licensed, triggering revenue-sharing payments," the analysts said.

  • Jihye Lee contributed to this article.

Write to Megan Cheah at megan.cheah@wsj.com

data.title: Trump Announces $17 Billion in Southeast Asia Deals
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong and Amanda Lee

The U.S. has secured a series of investment and trade deals across Southeast Asia as it seeks to expand its economic presence in the region.

President Trump announced more than $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments benefiting U.S. companies following a two-day state visit to the Philippines and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit, the White House said Wednesday.

Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced deals aimed at narrowing the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines by increasing Philippine imports of American energy and agricultural products, the White House said.

Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion deal to supply Philippine Airlines with up to 20 Boeing 787 aircraft. Washington also plans to pursue a military financing package worth more than $2 billion to provide the Philippines with U.S. defense equipment.

The U.S. and Thailand also made substantial progress toward a trade agreement that would eliminate tariffs on 99% of goods once signed and remove barriers to U.S. exports of vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals and agricultural products.

Thailand also plans to spend up to $123 million on U.S.-made High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems, the White House said.

In Indonesia, U.S.-based Latitude Energy and sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced talks on a $2 billion project to use American technology to improve the country's use of its coal resources.

U.S.-based Navajo Transitional Energy also signed a three-year, $100 million agreement to supply coal from its mine in southern Montana to Malaysia's TNB Fuel Services, a fuel procurement unit of utility Tenaga Nasional.

The announcements come as Southeast Asian economies grapple with higher U.S. tariffs while negotiating trade agreements with Washington.

Trade in goods and services between the U.S. and Asean totaled an estimated $686 billion in 2025, up 20.3% from 2024, according to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative.

Write to Ying Xian Wong at yingxian.wong@wsj.com and Amanda Lee at amanda.lee@wsj.com

data.title: SLS Stock Plunges Overnight As Sellas’ Discounted Share Offering Has Retail Bulls Crying Foul: ‘Crazy Low Price’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Sellas priced its $150 million share offering at $13, a 28% discount to Wednesday’s close.
  • Sellas plans to sell 11.54 million shares. Gross proceeds could reach $172.5 million if underwriters exercise their option in full.
  • The biotech firm plans to meet with the FDA and aims to file for vaccine approval in the first half of 2027.

Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) fell nearly 20% overnight heading into Thursday after the biotech firm priced its $150 million offering at a steep discount, frustrating investors who had welcomed its leukemia trial win a day earlier.

Why Sellas’ $13 Share Price Drew Attention

SLS stock entered the week trading at $7.47. Positive results from its Phase 3 leukemia trial sent the stock up 156% to $19.15 on Tuesday, before it gave back 6% on Wednesday. The rally allowed Sellas to price new shares about 74% above Monday’s close. For investors who bought after the results, though, the same deal gave new buyers a 28% discount, or nearly $5 a share, from Wednesday’s close.

Sellas plans to sell about 11.54 million new shares and expects the deal to close on Friday. The underwriters have 30 days to buy up to another 1.73 million shares, which would bring gross proceeds to $172.5 million if they exercise the option in full.

SLS Bulls Question Size Of The Discount

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS stayed ‘extremely bullish’ amid ‘extremely high’ message volume. Several users still supported the company or the decision to raise money. What drew their criticism was the price Sellas accepted so soon after the trial win.

One user questioned, “I guess the CEO thinks the company is only worth $13 per share? Crazy low price when the shares have been trading up to $20 every day.”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said, “$SLS the capital raise was absolutely 100% the right thing to do. Strongly disagree with this price though.”

View this Stocktwits post

A separate user said, “$SLS yeah, I know the price of the offering is disheartening. In the big scheme I won’t even remember this. What I can do is add 5% to my position to offset the dilution.”

What Comes Next For Sellas’ Leukemia Vaccine?

Behind Sellas’ recent rally was a survival benefit for leukemia patients with few treatment options left. In Sellas’ Phase 3 Regal trial, patients who received its experimental vaccine, Galinpepimut-S (GPS), lived a median of 24 months, compared with 14.7 months for those given the best available treatment. The trial met its main goal of improving survival in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who were in their second or later remission and could not undergo a stem cell transplant.

Sellas now plans to meet with the FDA and aims to file for approval in the first half of 2027. The offering would add to the $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents the company held at the end of September. Sellas said it would use the proceeds to fund clinical development, prepare for a potential launch and cover day-to-day operations.

SLS stock has surged 376% year-to-date.

data.title: Lenovo Maintains Revenue Momentum on AI-Fueled Hardware Demand
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Lenovo Group reported robust sales in the fiscal second quarter, on track to achieve its $100 billion annual revenue goal thanks to strong artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand.

Surging demand for AI servers and enterprise infrastructure has enabled the world's largest personal-computer maker to achieve better-than-expected results recently, offsetting a broader downturn in global PC shipments.

The company on Thursday said revenue for the three months ended September jumped 48% from a year earlier to $30.24 billion, beating market expectations.

Its adjusted net profit more than doubled to $1.36 billion, higher than analysts' estimate of $1.27 billion in a Visible Alpha poll. However, its bottom line was hit by a noncash fair-value loss arising from the revaluation of warrants, resulting in net loss of $640 million.

The company's infrastructure-solutions business, encompassing data-center hardware like AI servers, remained the biggest earnings driver. Segment revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, translating to operating profit of $1.09 billion.

Lenovo has been leveraging demand in the U.S., where the largest market opportunity for infrastructure currently resides. That could present challenges for its AI infrastructure business, especially after some cloud-service providers faced severe financial distress and Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections.

Shares of Lenovo have swung wildly in recent quarters, mirroring these concerns. The stock has wiped out the 50% advance it made in the three months ended September, trimming its gains for the year to about 80%.

Despite a memory crunch and rising consumer-electronics prices, Lenovo has handled the headwinds relatively well. Its intelligent-devices group, which includes PCs, smartphones and tablets, posted 15% revenue growth.

That came as global PC shipments fell 20% in July to September, according to industry tracker IDC. Continued supply constraints and the inventory pull-in earlier in the year, as vendors and channels rushed to stock up ahead of memory-chip-driven price hikes, left the quarter with little demand to draw on.

Lenovo remained the world's largest PC maker by shipments during the quarter, with a 23.8% market share.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: Anthropic's Trading Debut Faces High Uncertainty — Market Talk
data.description: Anthropic's debut faces high uncertainty, according to Morningstar's Malik Ahmed Khan in a research note. At $83 per share, Anthropic is coming to the market above its initial pricing range, but still below Morningstar's fair value estimates at $92 per share, or $1.7 trillion, the senior equity analyst points out. "Our valuation reflects the significant growth that we expect from AI adoption and Anthropic's position at the frontier of model development, particularly in areas such as coding and cybersecurity," the analyst says. Considerable uncertainty remains , he warns, noting the competitive landscape and economics of generative AI. He adds there are a wide range of potential outcomes as the company enters the public market. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
